title: Zero Mode Operators and Charge-Conjugation Defects in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall-Superconductor Heterostructures
abstract: We study zero modes bound to charge-conjugation defects in fractional quantum Hall-superconductor (FQH-SC) heterostructures built from Abelian and non-Abelian FQH states. Although the associated defects are well described by $G$-crossed braided tensor categories, a local operator description of their zero modes is not generally known. We generalize the bulk-to-boundary construction of localized zero mode operators to FQH-SCs with non-Abelian parent topological orders, mapping bulk Wilson operators in the folded theory to localized zero mode operators in the one-dimensional FQH-SC theory. This construction distinguishes zero mode anyons from the local zero mode operators that act on the defect Hilbert space and yields a generalized zero mode algebra. It also determines the fusion-channel dependence of tunneling: tunneling of zero mode operators probes bulk monodromy, while direct zero mode anyon transfer probes $G$-crossed associativity data. Applying this framework, we recover the $\mathbb{Z}_{2m}$ parafermion zero mode structure of fermionic Laughlin FQH-SCs at filling $ν=1/m$, obtain a $\mathbb{Z}_2^{(n)}\times\mathbb{Z}_N$ structure for generalized Moore-Read states at filling $ν=1/m$, with $N=2m$ for fermionic states and $N=m$ for bosonic states, and find a $\mathrm{Fib}\times\mathbb{Z}_N$ structure for the $k=3$ Read-Rezayi state at filling $ν=3/(3M+2)$, with $N=2(3M+2)$ for fermionic states and $N=(3M+2)/2$ for bosonic states. In the Read-Rezayi case, zero mode operator tunneling and direct zero mode anyon transfer yield distinct universal amplitude ratios between the neutral fusion channels, providing a characteristic signature of the underlying Fibonacci defect structure.
summary: This theoretical work develops a generalized framework to describe zero modes at defects in FQH-SC heterostructures, extending previous results to non-Abelian topological orders. By distinguishing between different physical processes—tunneling versus direct transfer—the authors derive unique signatures that characterize the underlying topological structure, notably confirming the Fibonacci nature of the Read-Rezayi state.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of finding a general local operator description for zero modes bound to charge-conjugation defects in non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall-Superconductor (FQH-SC) heterostructures.
main_result: The authors successfully construct a generalized zero mode algebra and predict distinct universal amplitude ratios for tunneling versus direct zero mode anyon transfer, providing a signature for the underlying topological order.
method: The methodology involves generalizing the bulk-to-boundary construction, mapping bulk Wilson operators to localized zero mode operators, and analyzing the resulting fusion-channel dependence.
model_or_system: The system studied is FQH-SC heterostructures built from Abelian and non-Abelian FQH states, where the superconducting proximity effect creates a charge-conjugation defect line.
key_observables: Zero mode anyons, the fusion-channel dependence of tunneling amplitudes, and the comparison between tunneling-probed bulk monodromy and direct transfer-probed $G$-crossed associativity data.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the superconducting proximity effect gaps the counter-propagating edges and that the defect structure is governed by $G$-crossed braided tensor categories.
figures_summary: The notes reference figures illustrating the physical setup (FQH edges coupled by superconductors), the mapping of Wilson operators, and the superconducting segment acting as a charge-conjugation defect line.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for a generalized zero mode construction, detailing the mapping from bulk operators, and then applying this framework to specific, highly correlated FQH states (Laughlin, MR, RR) to derive concrete algebraic structures and measurable signatures.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, measurable diagnostic (distinct amplitude ratios) to distinguish between different types of topological order (e.g., Fibonacci vs. Abelian) in superconducting quantum materials, which is highly relevant for realizing topological quantum computation.
